1000:03a0.purpose: MS C unsigned 32-bit division helper. Args on stack (dividend low,high then divisor low,high), result in DX:AX. 1000:2192.purpose: PC-speaker effect generated by bit-banging port 61h (the PIT channel 2 is set to divisor 0x003c, ~19.9 kHz, so only the gate bits matter). g_snd_delay_unit = g_cpu_speed/24 (0 if g_cpu_speed < 100). Because phase wraps, this is a square wave whose period is 65536/phase_step iterations and whose duty cycle drifts with the rising threshold (a sweep/buzz). With sound disabled only the delays run (same duration). Speaker gate is cleared at the end. Ghidra shows the five arguments reversed, e.g. FUN_2192(1,0x9c4,60000,1,0x157c) is play_sweep_noise(0x157c, 1, 60000, 0x9c4, 1). Return value is garbage.

1000:2322.name: disk_error_hook
1000:2322.purpose: The far error callback installed in g_error_hook; called by the file layer (file_exists, load_file, read_file_region ...) and the overlay manager whenever a file cannot be opened. It implements the original floppy-disk swapping logic. While running, g_error_hook is pointed at the RETF stub 1000:2320 so nested failures are ignored. letter = g_disk_drive_letters[g_cur_disk]. (1) If letter is known (!=0xff), g_cur_disk != g_disk_drive_set and the DOS current drive differs: just set_default_drive(letter), g_disk_drive_set = g_cur_disk, done. (2) Else if letter < 'C' and g_floppy_count > 1: swap A<->B (letter ^= 3), set_default_drive; if g_disk_drive_set != g_cur_disk, record it and return. (3) If letter is a hard-disk letter (>= 'C', != 0xff): force letter 'A', set_default_drive('A'), g_disk_drive_set = 0xff, done. (4) Otherwise prompt: if g_display_mode == 2 (graphics) set_draw_page(0), define_text_window(0, 6,12, 33,13) and fill_rect(40,88, 279,119) in colour 0 (a black message box); g_disk_drive_set = 0xff. In this (GOG) build the prompt itself is patched out: bytes 2405-2409 now do letter = get_current_drive_letter(); JMP 247d, skipping the dead code at 240a-2472 which printed '\nPlease insert the Ultima V Program/Britannia/Player Disk and press drive letter: ' (strings 0x545f..0x549c). Loop while g_disk_drive_letters[g_cur_disk] == 0xff: if set_default_drive(letter) succeeds break; else letter = to_upper(wait_key(0)). If the entry was unknown it is now set to letter ('B' also sets g_floppy_count = 2; when g_cur_disk == 3 and disk 1 is unknown, disk 1 gets the same letter). Finally: mode 0 -> put_char('\n'); mode 2 -> set_draw_page(1), define_text_window(0, 0,0, 39,24), copy_page(1,0) (restore screen from page 1). g_error_hook is restored to 1000:2322 before returning.

Cases: 0 walkers -> tile_walkable; 1 water-only -> tile_is_water; 2 flying/carpet -> tile in 0x60-0x6f, or water, or walkable; 3 horse -> walkable and tile != 0x8f and tile != 4 (swamp); 4 -> not water; 5 skiff -> for tiles 0x34-0x37 the facing bit (8 >> (mover_tile & 3)) of g_water_dir_mask[tile-0x34+16] must be set; otherwise the tile must be water, tiles < 0x60 are then allowed, and tiles 0x60-0x73 need the facing bit of g_water_dir_mask[tile-0x60]; 6 frigate -> tile <= 2 (deep/medium water) only; 7 -> tile == 4 only; 8 -> tile == 5 only; 9 -> tile == 1 only; 10 -> tile == 7 only; class 0xff or anything else -> 0. Callers pass g_transport_tile or a monster's tile as mover and a tile from the view buffer g_view_tiles (0xab02) or the map. Ghidra shows FUN_2c4c(tile, mover).

Each step is find_slot_with_tile_range(lo,hi,near). Returns the slot (0 only if all 23 slots hold tile 0xb5). Callers (CMDS, LOOKOBJ, MAINOUT, SJOG, TOWN) then fill the slot with set_monster_slot.

1000:3ef0.name: add_u8_capped
1000:3ef0.proto: void add_u8_capped(u8 *value /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int amount /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, unsigned max /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
1000:3ef0.purpose: Saturating byte add: if *value + amount < max then *value += amount, otherwise *value = max (so the result never exceeds max; reaching exactly max also clamps). Used for counters such as the moongate height (475a: add_u8_capped(&g_moongate_height,1,16)), stats, item counts (callers in CMDS/SHOPPES/SJOG/TALK/OUTSUBS and end_of_turn_party_update).

1000:3f14.name: add_i16_capped

1000:3f36.name: sub_u8_floor

1000:3f6e.name: view_tile_missile_passable
1000:3f6e.purpose: Looks up the terrain tile currently in the 11x11 view buffer at (row,col) (g_view_tiles[row*0x20+col]) and tests its bit in the 256-bit table g_missile_pass_bitmap (bit = 0x80>>(tile&7) of byte tile>>3). Returns nonzero when the bit is SET. In the DATA.OVL table the bit is clear for mountains/peaks (0x0c,0x0d), the settlement icons 0x12-0x15 and 0x19-0x1b, castle tiles 0x3a-0x3f, mast 0x42, pillar 0x46, stone walls 0x4d-0x4f, crenellations 0x50-0x55, window shelf 0x5a, 'strange walls' 0x70-0x7f, doors 0xb8/0xb9 and the collapsed dungeon entrance 0xdf, i.e. solid things a projectile/spell cannot pass; windows, arrow slits, water, trees pass. Only used by CAST (db30) and COMSUBS (f4be), i.e. for ranged attacks/spell lines of fire. Note: it tests the VIEW buffer (0 where an object sits), not the map.

0x6a14.name: g_missile_pass_bitmap
0x6a14.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a24: one bit per tile 0..255, set = projectiles/spell effects can pass through this tile

1000:4102.name: play_ambient_sounds
1000:4102.purpose: Called once per animation frame from refresh_map_view (5910) when animation is on. Scans the 11x11 cells around the party (map coords px-5..px+5, py-5..py+5; in combat, loc>=0x80, centre 5,5) and finds the NEAREST (squared distance, initial best 0x33) sound source, examining the MAP tile via get_map_tile(x,y): tiles 0xfa/0xfb (grandfather clock) -> type 1; 0xd4-0xd7 (waterfall) -> type 2; 0xd8-0xdb (unnamed animated tiles, almost certainly a fountain) -> type 3; a view cell holding an object (g_view_tiles==0) whose object tile is 0x15c-0x15f (the second 'minstrel' set = a musician) -> type 4. Then plays: type 1 (clock): if no chimes are pending (g_clock_chimes==0) or the frame counter g_ambient_frame is not 0 or 4, it ticks: beep(3000Hz,3) on frame 0, beep(2000Hz,3) on frame 4, nothing on other frames; if chimes are pending and the frame is 0 or 4 it plays a chime play_sweep_noise(phase_step=0xc2c,hold=1,count=2000,threshold=20000,threshold_step=-10) and (at the end) decrements g_clock_chimes. Type 2: play_random_tones(step=0x14,total=0x3c,max_freq=10000) (rushing water). Type 3: play_random_tones(10,0x1e,25000). Type 4: note = g_tune_sequence[g_tune_pos]; if nonzero plays play_sweep_noise(phase_step=g_tune_notes word at 0x6a34+2*note, hold=1,count=2000,threshold=20000,step=-10); then g_tune_pos++ wrapping to 0 after 0x34 (a 53-note loop; 0 = rest). Finally g_ambient_frame = (g_ambient_frame+1) & 7-ish (reset to 0 when >7). Ghidra shows the frequency constants as bogus string pointers (s__Have_a_pleasant_night_+0xd = 20000, s_Missed_+1 = 10000, 0x61a8 = 25000).

1000:43ae.name: play_tone_sweep
1000:43ae.proto: void play_tone_sweep(unsigned start_freq /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, unsigned end_freq /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int step /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int total /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
1000:43ae.purpose: Linear frequency glide on the PC speaker: for i = 0; i < total; i += step: start_tone(freq); delay_loop(speed_index=1,count=step); freq += (end_freq-start_freq)*step/total. Then stop_tone(). Used all over (CAST, CMDS, COMBAT, COMSUBS, DUNGEON, MAINOUT, SJOG, TALK, ZSTATS, ROOT 6936) for rising/falling effect sounds.

1000:4402.name: get_map_tile
1000:4402.purpose: Returns a pointer to the map byte for map coordinates (x,y) in the current map buffer; callers read or write through it. Three cases on g_location: (a) 0 = overworld (Britannia/Underworld): x -= g_chunk_x, y -= g_chunk_y, both masked & 0x1f, giving a position inside the 32x32 window of 4 cached 16x16 chunks at g_map (0x6608): chunk index c = (y>=16 ? 2 : 0) + (x>=16 ? 1 : 0) (coords reduced mod 16), address = 0x6608 + c*0x100 + (y&15)*16 + (x&15) - i.e. chunks are top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, each row-major 16x16 (the masking means coordinates wrap around the 256x256 world and the cache window). (b) 1..0x7f = town/dungeon level: if x or y is outside 0..31 returns the address of the last map byte 0x6a07 (map[31][31], used as the out-of-bounds filler); else 0x6608 + y*32 + x (the 32x32 map, save-RAM offset 0x1062). (c) >=0x80 = combat: returns g_light_map + y*0x20 + x (the combat map lives at 0xad14 with stride 32, no bounds check). 70 callers across all modules.

1000:44b8.name: cycle_tile_anim_map
1000:44b8.purpose: Advances the terrain animation remap table g_tile_anim_map (256 bytes, entry t = tile actually drawn for map tile t). Every call: entries 0xd4..0xd7 (waterfall) are incremented and wrapped back to 0xd4 when they reach 0xd8; entries 0xd8..0xdb (fountain) likewise wrap at 0xdc. On every second call (g_anim_frame_counter bit 0 set): entries 0x80..0x83 (pendulum) are XORed with 1 (swing), entries 0xec..0xef (standard of Britannia) cycle within 0xec..0xef; and on every fourth call (bit 1 also set) entries 0xfa..0xfd (grandfather clock, bellows) are XORed with 1. Then g_anim_frame_counter++. Called only from animate_monsters (4552), i.e. once per animated frame. The initial table in DATA.OVL is all zero; something at start-up (part 4 / overlay code) must fill it with the identity mapping.

0xb11e.meaning: display tile for each terrain tile 0..255 (identity except the animated groups); used by draw_map_view

0x6a7e.name: g_anim_frame_counter
0x6a7e.meaning: frame counter for terrain animation (bit0 = every 2nd frame, bit1 = every 4th)

1000:4552.name: animate_monsters
1000:4552.purpose: Per-frame sprite animation of every non-empty slot of g_monster_table (32 x 8 bytes), driven by the slot's byte +6 (Value 2): low nibble = delay counter (0xf = frozen, never animates), high nibble = position in an animation script. base = tile0 & 0xfc (the 4-frame group); script row = g_anim_script_index[(base-0x34)>>2] (one byte per tile group from 0x134 upward; e.g. guards->5, sharks->9, bats/ghosts/slimes/orcs/pythons/headless/daemons->1, spiders->6, mimics->4, gazers->3, gargoyles->10, dragons/trolls->7, mongbats->2, corpsers->8, most others 0). If the delay nibble is nonzero it is just decremented. If it is 0 the slot animates only when: anim tile (+1) is not 0, 0x1d or 0x1e, base > 0x33 (objects, vehicles and chairs below 0x134 never animate), base != 0xe8 (fields), base != 0xb4 (shards/crown/sceptre/amulet), and (base == 0x5c (musician) or base == 0xa8 (mimic chest) or rand_range(0,255) >= 0x80 i.e. 50%). It then interprets g_anim_scripts[row][pos] in a loop: 1..4 -> anim tile = base+cmd-1, pos++, stop; 5 -> 75%: pos++ and continue; 25%: anim tile = tile0 (frame 0), then for the musician pos++ and stop, else keep pos and set delay 6, stop; 6 -> 25%: pos++ continue, 75%: fall into 0; 0 -> pos = 0, continue; 7 -> pos = 2, continue; any other (0x80|n) -> delay = n (cmd+0x80 as a byte), pos++, stop. The new state byte is pos*16+delay. After the loop over all 32 slots it calls cycle_tile_anim_map (44b8) and ROOT 6fd6 (driver entry 32 with CF=0, AX=g_font_segs[0] - the driver-side part of the per-frame animation, see part 4). Callers: refresh_map_view, CAST2 e64c, FONT e4dc.

0x5848.name: g_moonstone_z

1000:475a.name: update_moongates
1000:475a.purpose: Called every animated frame (from refresh_map_view, non-combat). Decides the moongate tile: by day (5 <= g_hour < 20) g_moongate_height is decremented (floor 0) and the tile is 0xdc (moon gate) while height > 0, or 5 (grass) once it has shrunk to 0; at night the height is incremented up to 16 and the tile is 0xdc. Then for each of the 8 moonstones that moonstone_on_current_map reports as buried here, writes that tile into the map at (x,y) via get_map_tile, ORs 2 into g_view_dirty, and if the map byte actually changed calls rebuild_light_map (5e4a; a moongate is a light source). So all buried moonstones become moongates at night and the gates visibly grow/shrink over 16 frames; draw_map_view renders a partial gate while 1 <= height <= 15.

0x5887.meaning: save 0x2E1: moongate height 0..16 (frames of the rise/shrink animation)

1000:47f4.name: moongate_travel
1000:47f4.purpose: Teleports the party to the burial place of moonstone number `moonstone` (0..7, chosen from the moon phase). Returns 0 immediately if that stone is in inventory (g_moonstone_loc == 0xff). If the party is currently in the overworld: select_disk(1), wait until BRIT.DAT exists, and save the monster table (0x100 bytes at g_monster_table) to the overworld object file named by OUTSUBS a5f8 ('BRIT.OOL' when g_party_z==0 else 'UNDER.OOL'). Sets g_party_x/y/z from the stone. Then: if both the destination loc and the current loc are settlements (1..0x20): g_location = dest and TOWN_93c0(1) loads/initialises that town; if both are 0 (overworld, incl. Britannia<->Underworld via z): g_location = 0, loads the monster table back from the .OOL file for the new level (load_file_region(name, g_monster_table, 0x100, 0)) and MAINOUT_81d0 reloads the chunk cache; any other combination just keeps g_location and the new coordinates (not expected in practice). Returns 1. Callers: enter_moongate (48a8) and CAST cc70.

1000:48a8.name: enter_moongate
1000:48a8.purpose: Called by the MAINOUT and TOWN main loops after a move. If the map tile under the party is 0xdc (moon gate): animate_wait(1); play_sweep_noise(5900,1,2000,20000,2) (teleport sound); temporarily sets g_transport_tile = 0x16 (sprite 0x116, a blank - so the party is not drawn) and runs tile_transition_effect(0xdc, 5, 5) (dissolve of the gate at the centre cell), then g_transport_tile = 0, animate_wait(1), and shrinks the gate with draw_effect_frame(h,5,5) for h = 15 down to 1 with wait_ticks(2) between frames. The map byte at the party position is set to 5 (grass), g_view_dirty |= 2, draw_tile(5,5,5). Then: if g_hour == 0 and g_minute < 10 (first ten minutes after midnight) it restores the transport tile and returns 1 (the caller then performs the special midnight destination via FUN_1778_02ea); otherwise phase = g_trammel_phase if hour < 12 else g_felucca_phase (characters '0'..'7'), moongate_travel(phase-'0'), restore the transport tile, return 0. Returns 0 when not standing on a gate.

1000:4f7c.purpose: Advances the game clock by `minutes` and recomputes the light level. If g_minute > 59: minute -= 60, g_hours_until_heal -= 1 (floor 0), hour++. If hour > 23: hour = 0 and a new day starts: each of the 3 Shadowlords (g_shadowlord_loc, < 0x80 = not destroyed) moves to a random town rand_range(1,8) that is neither the party's current location nor any Shadowlord's current town (re-rolled until valid); day++. If day > 28: the three g_harvest_day bytes, g_skull_key_day and g_unk_5959 are zeroed, day = 1, every character record's months-at-inn (+0x17) is incremented while < 25, month++, and if month > 13 month = 1 and g_year++. draw_status_window() after any hour change. (2) Light (skipped if g_light_level > 0x32): in Ararat (0x19), when g_party_z >= 0x80, or when hour < 5 or hour > 19 the level is 2 (night: only the 3x3 around the party); hour 5 uses g_dawn_light_table[minute/10] (2,5,10,20,34,49) and hour 19 the same table with (59-minute)/10 (dusk); other hours 0x32 (full view). Then a light spell forces at least 0x12 and a torch at least 10. If the level changed, g_view_dirty = 1. (3) If the hour changed from g_hour_prev: draw_sky_strip() when not in a dungeon and not in the underworld, and g_clock_chimes = hour mod 12 (12 at midnight). (4) In a settlement (1..0x20) calls ROOT 71aa (driver entry 36 with AX=2, BL=hour, BH=minute - a time-of-day hook in the driver, see part 4). 19 callers (all main loops, camping, combat...).

1000:51b8.name: place_object_in_view
1000:51b8.proto: void place_object_in_view(int col /*param_5,[bp+c]*/, int row /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, int x /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int y /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int tile /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
1000:51b8.purpose: Stores an object/creature sprite (tile is 0x100-relative) into view cell (row,col) for map position (x,y), applying the furniture/terrain substitutions. Fast path: if tile is not a creature-like sprite (0x1c avatar on foot, 0x12-0x15 mounted party, 0x28-0x2b skiff, or >= 0x40 NPC/monster) it is stored as is. Otherwise under = *get_map_tile(x,y): 0xec (standard of Britannia) or 0x0a (tropical forest) -> return, the creature is hidden; 0x57 (a crenellation) -> g_view_tiles[row][col] = 0x38 (gargoyle statue) and return (nothing stored in the object layer: gargoyles perched on the wall look like statues); 0x6a/0x6b (bridge over a river) -> sea monsters (tile & 0xf0 == 0x80) and skiffs (tile & 0xfc == 0x28) are hidden under the bridge, others stored as is. For tiles < 0x80 (people) further substitutions: chair 0x92 -> if the tile south (x,y+1) is a table with food 0x9a or 0x9c, tile = 0x34 + random_sitting_frame() (eating), else 0x32 (seated); chair 0x90 -> if north (x,y-1) is 0x9b/0x9c, 0x38 + frame else 0x30; chairs 0x91/0x93 -> 0x30 + (under & 3); stocks 0x84 -> 0x60 + frame, manacles 0x85 -> 0x64 + frame (prisoners); mirror 0x9d/0x9e -> 0x3c + frame; bed 0xab -> 0x1a (occupied bed); ladders 0xc8/0xc9 -> 0x17/0x18. If no substitution matched and the tile north of the creature is a mirror 0x9d and row > 0, the view cell above (g_view_tiles[row-1][col]) is set to 0x9e (mirror showing a reflection). Finally g_view_objects[row][col] = tile and g_view_tiles[row][col] = 0 (meaning 'draw the object layer here'). Only caller: place_objects_in_view.

1000:5394.name: place_objects_in_view
1000:5394.purpose: Merges the monster/object table into the 11x11 view. Outside combat it first stores the party into slot 0 (x,y,z from g_party_x/y/z, tile0 = anim tile = g_transport_tile) and applies a distance rule to the view terrain: a cell holding 0xdd (a 'parched desert' variant) whose squared distance from the centre (view_dist_sq, 6ff0) is > 5 becomes plain desert 0x1c, and a 0x1c cell within distance 5 becomes 0xdd (something in the desert that is only visible close up - presumably the sand-trap marking). Then for every slot from 31 down to 0 with tile0 != 0: outside combat the slot must be on the party's level and within the view (col = x-(px-5), row = y-(py-5), both <= 10); in combat col=x,row=y. The slot is skipped if its anim tile is 0 or the view cell is 0xff (dark) or 0x87 (archway - things under an arch are hidden). Then: fields (tile0 & 0xfc == 0xe8) and corpses (tile0 0x1e/0x1f) are stored only if the cell has no object yet (view != 0); anim tiles 0x1d/0x1e always overwrite the cell (object = anim tile, view = 0); a musician (tile0 == 0x5c) standing on chair 0x92 is stored as itself, otherwise drawn as anim tile - 8 (the 0x154 merchant-like sprite) through place_object_in_view; everything else goes through place_object_in_view(col,row,x,y,anim_tile). Since lower slots are processed last, slot 0 (the party) wins conflicts. Callers: refresh_map_view, CAST c6cc, CAST2 e64c.

1000:5a28.name: flood_visibility
1000:5a28.proto: void flood_visibility(int radius /*param_7,[bp+10]*/, int y0 /*param_6*/, int x0 /*param_5*/, int row_base /*param_4; -111 = view mode*/, int col_base /*param_3*/, int stride /*param_2, unused*/, u8 *dest /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
1000:5a28.purpose: Breadth-first line-of-sight flood over the 11x11 view area. (x0,y0) is the map position of view cell (0,0) relative to the chunk origin (get_map_tile is called with (x0+col+g_chunk_x, y0+row+g_chunk_y)). dest[(row_base+row)*0x20 + col_base + col] receives the result; the stride argument is ignored (0x20 hard-coded). Two modes: row_base == -111 (0xff91) selects VIEW mode (called by build_lit_view with dest = g_view_tiles, row_base becomes 0); any other value is LIGHT-MAP mode (called by rebuild_light_map with dest = g_light_map and row/col_base = source-5, g_view_tiles used as a scratch 'visited' grid). Algorithm: a 256-entry queue of (row,col) on the stack starts with the centre (5,5), whose dest cell is set to the map tile; pop cells and visit the 8 neighbours in order W,SW,S,SE,E,NE,N,NW, skipping those outside 0..10. A neighbour is skipped if already visited: view mode: dest cell != 0xff; light mode: g_view_tiles cell == 0 or row_base+row > 31, else it is marked by writing 0. For a visited cell: tile = map tile, d = view_dist_sq(row,col). If d <= radius the cell is lit: dest = tile. Otherwise, view mode: if the tile is opaque (tile_transparent(d,tile) false) it is shown (dest = tile) only when the queue-head cell's dest is nonzero AND both the parent and this cell are lit in g_light_map, else dest = 0xff (dark) and tile = 0xff; if transparent it is shown when the cell lies in the 32x32 map and g_light_map says it is lit, else dest = 0 (dark). Light mode beyond radius: tile = 0xff, nothing written. Finally if tile_transparent(d, tile) the cell is pushed so the flood continues through it (windows/doors with windows are transparent only when adjacent, d == 1). Net effect: everything within the light radius plus anything lit by a map light source that has an unobstructed path is visible.

0xab02.meaning: dest in view mode / visited grid in light mode

0xad14.name: g_light_map
0xad14.meaning: 0 = unlit, else lit (tile value) - consulted in view mode, written in light mode

0x6aa8.name: g_view_dist_sq
0x6aa8.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6ab8: squared distance from the view centre for one quadrant (mirrored by view_dist_sq 6ff0): 0 at (5,5) .. 50 at the corner

0x6a86.name: g_opaque_tiles
0x6a86.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a96: tiles that block sight (trees 09/0a, mountains 0c/0d, walls 4d-4f, 5a, odd door 97, doors b8/b9, fireplace bc, d0-d3, f8, wall fe, darkness ff) - used by tile_transparent (5dfe)

1000:5a28.notes: Helper semantics (6ff0 = view_dist_sq(row,col) returning g_view_dist_sq for the mirrored quadrant, 0 outside 0..10; 5dfe = tile_transparent(dist_sq, tile): tiles 0x4a arrow slit, 0x4b window, 0xba/0xbb doors with window, 0x98 odd door transparent only when dist_sq == 1, otherwise transparent iff not in g_opaque_tiles) belong to part 4 but were read to make this description. The opaque-beyond-radius rule in view mode depends on dest cells of the queue head being nonzero, i.e. already shown.

1000:5d0a.name: build_lit_view
1000:5d0a.proto: void build_lit_view(int light /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, int px_rel /*param_3*/, int py_rel /*param_2*/, int size /*param_1, always 11, unused*/)
1000:5d0a.purpose: Rebuilds g_view_tiles from the map around the party. (px_rel,py_rel) = party position minus the chunk origin. Fills the 11x11 view with 0xff (darkness). If light > 0: flood_visibility(light, py_rel-5, px_rel-5, -111 (view mode), 0, 0x20, g_view_tiles), then every view cell still 0 (visited but dark) becomes 0xff. If light < 0 (only reachable from CAST2 e64c): the 11x11 cells are copied straight from the map (full visibility, no line of sight). light == 0 leaves everything dark. Called by refresh_map_view when g_view_dirty is set.

1000:6f9e.name: driver_tile_patch_special
1000:6f9e.proto: void driver_tile_patch_special(int n /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)  /* pascal: AX = n+3 */
1000:6f9e.purpose: Calls driver entry 36 (offset 0x6c) with AX = n+3, i.e. tile-set patch command 3 (n=0, from DNGLOOK_b3c0) or 4 (n=1, from ENDGAME_a8d8). In EGA.DRV command 3 swaps the two middle bytes of every 4-byte group in the bitmaps of tiles 5, 0x1e, 0x1f, 0x4c, 0xca, 0x20-0x26, 0x30-0x37 and 0x60-0x6f (a plane/colour swap of those tiles - a visual effect, exact look not determined); command 4 is a further variant (at EGA.DRV 0x2c4e, not examined). Ghidra mis-decompiled the body (it shows a call through a string); the listing bytes are MOV AX,[BP+4]; ADD AX,3; MOV [5350],0x6c; CALLF [5350]; RET 2.
1000:6f9e.notes: Tile-set offsets in the driver: tile t at t*0x80 in the segment stored at EGA.DRV cs:0x206.

1000:6fbc.name: driver_tile_patch
1000:6fbc.proto: void driver_tile_patch(int cmd /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)  /* pascal: AX = cmd */
1000:6fbc.purpose: Driver entry 36 with AX = cmd. cmd 0 (DNGLOOK_aefc, when it also sets g_tiles_patched=1): the driver saves 8 bytes of tile bitmap at tile-set offsets 0x6470 (row 14 of tile 0xc8) and 0x8bf0 (row 14 of tile 0x117) into its own buffer and overwrites each with the tile's row 0 (offset -0x70). cmd 1 (run_encounter after combat, when g_tiles_patched): restores the saved bytes. Net effect: temporarily alters two tile images while inside certain dungeon rooms. cmd 2 is driver_set_clock_tile (71aa); 3/4 see 6f9e.
1000:6fbc.notes: Which images tiles 0xc8 / 0x117 are is not confirmed (0x117 is drawn for ladders by place_object_in_view).

1000:6fd6.name: driver_animate_tile_bitmaps
1000:6fd6.purpose: Calls driver entry 32 (offset 0x60) with the carry flag clear and AX = g_font_segs[0] (the IBM.CH font segment; the CF=1 path of the same entry is draw_effect_frame). In EGA.DRV the CF=0 path mutates the tile bitmaps in place each frame: 32 iterations write a pseudo-random byte (same LCG as rand_range, private seed in the driver) into 9 positions of each 4-byte group of the four tiles at tile-set offset 0xf400 (tiles 0x1e8-0x1eb, i.e. sprites 0xe8-0xeb - fire/flame-like sprites), then rotates the rows of the tile at offset 0x80 (tile 1, deep water) by one row (block moves of 0x3c words) and continues with further tiles (offset 0x100...). Called once per animation frame by animate_monsters after cycle_tile_anim_map; it is the 'noise and scroll' half of the terrain animation and consumes the driver's RNG, not g_rand_seed.

0x539c.name: g_font_segs
0x539c.meaning: [0] passed in AX (apparently unused by the EGA driver)

1000:6fd6.notes: For the port: implement as a per-frame mutation of the water and fire tile images; exact pixel pattern only matters cosmetically.

1000:6ff0.name: view_dist_sq
1000:6ff0.purpose: Squared distance of view cell (a,b) from the view centre (5,5) via the quadrant table: if either coordinate >= 11 returns 0; coordinates > 5 are mirrored (10-v); returns g_view_dist_sq[b][a] (DATA.OVL 0x6aa8, 6x6 bytes, x*x+y*y). Symmetric, so argument order does not matter. Used by flood_visibility (light radius / adjacency test) and place_objects_in_view (desert tile swap).

1000:7040.name: draw_light_beam_frame
1000:7040.proto: void draw_light_beam_frame(int frame /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, int on /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int x /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int y /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
1000:7040.purpose: Writes one orientation of the rotating light beam into the town light map: for the 16 (dx,dy) signed byte pairs of pattern row (frame % 16) in g_light_beam_pattern (0x1f7e, 16 rows x 32 bytes) sets g_light_map[(y+dy)*32 + x+dx] to 0xff when on==1, else 0. No bounds checks (row wrap-around is possible near map edges; the source sits well inside the map). 0xff counts as 'lit' for the visibility flood.

0x1f7e.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x1f8e: 16 beam orientations x 16 relative cells (dx,dy); unused pairs are (0,0)

1000:7040.notes: The wiki marks file 0x1f7e-0x21da as unknown; the first 16 bytes before the pattern are the shrine x/y lists.

1000:70a6.name: animate_light_beam
1000:70a6.purpose: Per-frame rotating light beam (lighthouse style) in settlements; called by refresh_map_view outside combat. If g_light_level >= 0x32 (full daylight) or there is no beam source (g_beam1_x == -1): g_beam_frame = 0xff (idle) and return. Otherwise g_view_dirty = 1 and: if the frame is 0xff, start: frame = 0 and draw frames 0,1,2 ON at source 1 (0x217e/0x2180) and, if g_beam2_x != -1, at source 2 (0x2182/0x2184); else erase frame f at both sources, f++, draw frame f+2 at both. Frames wrap 16 -> 0 (the pattern index is taken mod 16 anyway). So three adjacent orientations are lit at a time and the beam sweeps one step per map refresh. Sources are set by TOWN_85d8 (first two '*' (0x2a) tiles found in the town map, -1 if none) and OUTSUBS (the 0x1b tile in the cached overworld chunks).

0x217e.name: g_beam1_x
0x217e.meaning: RAM-ish in DATA.OVL (file 0x218e): x of light source 1, -1 none

0x24e6.name: g_view_dirty
0x24e6.meaning: set every frame while the beam runs

1000:70a6.notes: Identification as the lighthouse beam is inferred from the rotating 16-orientation pattern and night-only gating; tile names 0x2a/0x1b are not in the references.

1000:71ca.name: scroll_rect_up
1000:71ca.proto: void scroll_rect_up(int x1 /*[bp+c] AX*/, int y1 /*[bp+a] BX*/, int x2 /*[bp+8] CX*/, int y2 /*[bp+6] DX*/, int rows /*[bp+4] SI*/)

1000:7234.name: dos_read_region
1000:7234.proto: unsigned dos_read_region(const char *name /*[bp+a]*/, void *buf /*[bp+8]*/, unsigned count /*[bp+6]*/, unsigned offset /*[bp+4]*/)
1000:7234.purpose: Assembly DOS wrapper used by load_file_region (256e): g_last_dos_error = 0; INT 21h/3Dh open (AL=2 read/write); if the open fails or the INT 24h handler flagged an error (g_last_dos_error != 0) -> error; if offset != 0, INT 21h/42h lseek to CX:DX = 0:offset (16-bit offsets only, enough for the 0x1060-byte save and 0x400-byte map pages); count 0 means 0xffff; INT 21h/3Fh read into DS:buf; INT 21h/3Eh close. Returns the number of bytes read; on any failure stores the DOS error code in g_last_dos_error, calls the far error hook g_error_hook and returns 0 (load_file_region then retries).

1000:7296.name: dos_write_file
1000:7296.proto: unsigned dos_write_file(const char *name /*[bp+8]*/, const void *buf /*[bp+6]*/, unsigned count /*[bp+4]*/)
1000:7296.purpose: Assembly DOS wrapper used by save_file_region (25d8): INT 21h/3Ch create/truncate (attributes 0), INT 21h/40h write count bytes from DS:buf, INT 21h/3Eh close (flags preserved around the close). Success: g_last_dos_error = 0, returns bytes written. Failure of create or write: g_last_dos_error = DOS code, calls g_error_hook, returns 0.
1000:7296.notes: RET 6. Last function of ROOT; 72d5-72df padding.

0xa452.name: g_crt_rterr_msgs
0xa452.meaning: MS C run-time error message table (R6000 stack overflow, R6001 null pointer assignment, ... , "run-time error "), terminated by id -1; ends at the BSS start 0xa524

0xa524.name: g_bss_start
0xa524.meaning: start of BSS: zeroed by crt0 (0xa524..0xbd3f) so every RAM global starts at 0; DATA.OVL holds zeros here (wiki "0xa530 unknown 0x1820"). Named RAM tables inside: 0xa9bd disk state, 0xa9fc monster-table backup, 0xab02 view tiles, 0xac64 view objects, 0xad14 light/combat map, 0xb11c OOL pointer, 0xb11e tile anim map, 0xb21e OOL buffer, 0xba14 combat roster, 0xbb14.. dungeon RAM bytes

0xa9bd.name: g_cur_disk
0xa9bd.meaning: index of the game disk currently required (0..5; 2 and 5 alias 1)

0xa9be.name: g_display_mode
0xa9be.meaning: 0 = text mode, 1 = intro/loading, 2 = graphics mode (affects how prompts are shown)

0xa9c2.name: g_floppy_count
0xa9c2.meaning: number of floppy drives known (2 once drive B is used)

0xa9c8.name: g_disk_drive_letters
0xa9c8.meaning: drive letter for each game disk, 0xff = not yet known (DATA.OVL initial 0)

0xa9ce.name: g_sound_enabled
0xa9ce.meaning: nonzero = PC speaker sound on (toggled by a command, set to 1 by INTRO)

0xa9fc.name: g_monster_table_backup_a9fc
0xa9fc.meaning: copy of g_monster_table for the duration of combat (part 2 named slot 1 of it at 0xaa04)

0xaa04.name: g_monster_table_backup_aa04
0xaa04.meaning: g_monster_table_backup_a9fc slot 1 onward (base 0xa9fc; part 2 named slot 1 here) - copy of the monster table made by run_camp_scene (base 0xa9fc; 0xaa04 = slot 1)

0xab02.name: g_view_tiles
0xab02.meaning: terrain tile of each view cell (row stride 0x20); 0 = an object is drawn there instead (see g_view_objects), 0xff = darkness

0xac64.name: g_view_objects
0xac64.meaning: object/NPC tile (0x100-relative) drawn at each view cell when g_view_tiles is 0 (row stride 0x10)

0xad14.name: g_light_map
0xad14.meaning: RAM: in towns the light map built by rebuild_light_map (0 = unlit, else the tile); in combat (loc>=0x80) the 11x11 combat map (stride 0x20)

0xb11c.name: g_ool_buffer_ptr
0xb11c.meaning: near pointer to the SAVED.OOL buffer (0xb21e)

0xb11e.name: g_tile_anim_map
0xb11e.meaning: display tile for each terrain tile 0..255 (identity except the animated groups); used by draw_map_view

0xb31e.name: g_ool_buffer_under
0xb31e.meaning: second half of g_ool_buffer: UNDER.OOL image (Underworld object list) written by main() after a game is loaded

0xba14.name: g_combat_roster
0xba14.meaning: combat participants: +2 flags (0x80 party member, 1/2/4/8 state bits), +3 party index or monster char, +4 monster-table slot, +6 x, +7 y (RAM only)

0xba15.name: g_roster_initiative
0xba15.meaning: roster +1: dexterity for party members, stat0 +/-3 for monsters

0xba16.name: g_roster_flags
0xba16.meaning: g_combat_roster +2 flags: 0x80 party member, 0x20 inactive, 0x10/0x04 (COMBAT), 0x01 charmed; stride 8

0xba17.name: g_roster_member
0xba17.meaning: g_combat_roster entry +3: party member index for party-side entries (monster type for monsters), stride 8

0xba18.name: g_roster_slot
0xba18.meaning: roster +4: monster-table slot of this combatant

0xbb14.name: g_dungeon_wall_tile
0xbb14.meaning: RAM: wall tile of the current dungeon style, set by DUNGEON_8ffe (md part 4)

0xbb15.name: g_dungeon_floor_tile
0xbb15.meaning: RAM: floor tile of the current dungeon style (0x45 or 5), set by DUNGEON_8ffe

0xbb16.name: g_tiles_patched
0xbb16.meaning: RAM: 1 when DNGLOOK applied driver_tile_patch(0); restored with command 1 after combat

0xbb17.name: g_dungeon_flags
0xbb17.meaning: RAM byte after g_tiles_patched: dungeon flags (DUNGEON overlay) (md part 4)

0xbb18.name: g_intro_flag_bb18
0xbb18.meaning: RAM byte used by INTRO (md part 4); meaning not determined

0xbd40.name: g_stack
0xbd40.meaning: end of the DATA.OVL image (file size 0xbd50 -> DGROUP 0xbd40). crt0 sets SP = 0xbd3e per the ROOT analysis while ARCHITECTURE.md places BSS+stack at 0xbd50..0xc53f with the stack top at 0xc540; the stack grows down from whichever top the loader chooses - leave 0x800 bytes above the image
